english.notes:
(i) Where the assault occurs when the offender has in his/her possession a firearm officers should also consider charging with an offence under the Firearms Act 1968. See H1162, H2142 and H2218.
(ii) Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. While 'assault with intent to rob' does not attract a mandatory life sentence, if the offender was charged with an appropriate firearms offence (see Note (1) above) - provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
(iii) Officers should carefully check an offender's previous convictions. While 'assault with intent to rob' does not attract a mandatory life sentence, if the offender was charged with an appropriate firearms offence (see Note (i) above) - A prior conviction for an offence listed in Schedule 15 to the Sentencing Act 2020, may render the convicted person liable to a mandatory life sentence in relation to a second offence listed under that Schedule, as per section 273 (offender aged 18 or over but under 21 when convicted of the second offence or section 283 (offender aged 21 or over).
